proof:
Source. Step 4 of the supplied proof of local_comparison (the inequalities (∗)), with the positive denominators cleared at the end.

1. (Continuity at 0.) For ε < 1 put φ(ε) := ((1 + ε)/(1 − ε))^{m+1}. φ is continuous at ε = 0. Numerator and denominator are continuous, the denominator is 1 ≠ 0 at ε = 0, and powers of functions continuous at a point are continuous there. Also φ(0) = 1 < t. Hence, shrinking δ if necessary, there is δ ∈ (0, 1] with φ(ε) < t whenever |ε| < δ. Every such ε satisfies ε < 1, so φ(ε) is defined.

2. (Choice of ε.) Put ε := δ/2. Then 0 < ε < δ ≤ 1, so 0 < ε < 1 and φ(ε) < t. In filter language: {ε : φ(ε) < t} is a neighbourhood of 0, and (0, 1) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT), so their intersection belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 and is nonempty. Fix this ε and put q := (1 + ε)/(1 − ε). Then q^{m+1} = φ(ε) < t.

3. (Comparison with q.) We have 0 < 1 − ε ≤ 1 ≤ 1 + ε.
 (a) 1 + ε ≤ q: since 1 − ε ≤ 1 and 1 + ε > 0, (1 + ε)(1 − ε) ≤ 1 + ε; dividing by 1 − ε > 0 gives 1 + ε ≤ (1 + ε)/(1 − ε) = q.
 (b) 1/(1 − ε) ≤ q: since 1 ≤ 1 + ε and 1 − ε > 0.
 All of 1 + ε, 1/(1 − ε) and q are positive.

4. (First inequality.) Products and natural powers of nonnegative reals are monotone. So by 3, (1 + ε)^m·(1/(1 − ε)) ≤ q^m·q = q^{m+1} < t. Thus (1 + ε)^m/(1 − ε) ≤ t. Multiplying by 1 − ε > 0 gives (1 + ε)^m ≤ t·(1 − ε).

5. (Second inequality.) Likewise (1 + ε)·(1/(1 − ε))^m ≤ q·q^m = q^{m+1} < t. Since (1/(1 − ε))^m = 1/(1 − ε)^m and (1 − ε)^m > 0, this says (1 + ε)/(1 − ε)^m ≤ t. Multiplying by (1 − ε)^m gives 1 + ε ≤ t·(1 − ε)^m.

6. Steps 2, 4 and 5 give 0 < ε < 1 and both inequalities. Nothing depends on the size of m; for m = 0 the inequalities read 1 ≤ t(1 − ε) and 1 + ε ≤ t. ∎
key_steps: ε ↦ ((1+ε)/(1−ε))^{m+1} is continuous at 0 with value 1 < t, so some ε ∈ (0,1) has q^{m+1} < t for q := (1+ε)/(1−ε).
(1+ε)^m/(1−ε) ≤ q^{m+1} < t and (1+ε)/(1−ε)^m ≤ q^{m+1} < t; clearing the positive denominators gives (1+ε)^m ≤ t(1−ε) and 1+ε ≤ t(1−ε)^m.
